question: Can protecting the public decision improve release and preserve the marginal value of targeted evidence in the delegates' section?
anchor: On 3 November 2021 the Security Council adopted France's draft S/2021/913 unanimously (15–0–0) as resolution 2604 (2021). Acting under Chapter VII, it authorized Member States acting through or in cooperation with the EU to continue EUFOR ALTHEA for twelve months. The resolution made no decision on the civilian High Representative's appointment or office.
instruction: Write only the delegates' statements section of a documentary record. An editor supplies the decision separately. In at most 65 words total, use two short paragraphs, one per delegation. Use the provided notes exclusively. Attribute each position to the speaker's delegation, preserving any conditions and the stated reasons attached to that position. Combine a supplement only where it supports the same speaker. Keep separate claims and their reasons distinct. Omit details the notes do not support. Output only the two paragraphs.
hold_fixed: Four archived note sets and original checkpoint, four-call path including reused calls, final generation cap, 120-word record limit, criterion weights and release guards.
primary: Run the same writer and frozen public rendering across all paths. Compare grounded note uptake and the 30 points for delegation statements independently of the 40 supplied decision points.
limits: One exposed case. This changes the writing interface and prompt together. The public passage is supplied intervention text. The trial measures conditional record quality from archived policy traces.
